title: On Bowing to the oldest man first
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：bow　|　正文 351 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bow 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the cook ① bowed to the oldest man first year after year, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② bows to the oldest man first for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ bow to the oldest man first at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ bowed to the oldest man first before — a line in the menu for September 1976 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Bowing to the oldest man first year after year, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ bow his head before the crowd for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Bow his head before the crowd at once and never mention it again.

By 1989 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ bows his head before the crowd year after year every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ bowed to the oldest man first again when nobody else would.

⑩ To bow to the oldest man first, my mother said in 1994, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody bows to the oldest man first for the whole place again and somebody must bow to the oldest man first year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 鞠躬（一般过去式 bowed to the oldest man first：1982 年厨子头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 鞠躬（一般现在 bows to the oldest man first：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 鞠躬（不定式 to bow to the oldest man first：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 鞠躬（过去完成时 had bowed to the oldest man first：1976 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 鞠躬（动名词 bowing to the oldest man first 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 低下（bow his head before the crowd：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去低下在众人面前低下头）
G. v. 低下（bow his head before the crowd：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 鞠躬（后段两处：新来的客人照例 bows his head before the crowd，而母亲又一次 bowed to the oldest man first）

answers.why: bow 意为“鞠躬”，1982 年厨子年年地鞠躬先向最年长的那位鞠躬，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 bowed。
bow 意为“鞠躬”，自那以后厨子替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 bows。
bow 意为“鞠躬”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯鞠躬先向最年长的那位鞠躬”，此处为不定式 to bow to the oldest man first。
bow 意为“鞠躬”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1989 年之前就有人鞠躬过，故用过去完成时 had bowed。
bow 意为“鞠躬”，厨子说“鞠躬先向最年长的那位鞠躬这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 bowing to the oldest man first 作主语。
bow 意为“低下”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去低下在众人面前低下头”，should ever 之后用原形 bow his head before the crowd。
bow 意为“低下”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻低下在众人面前低下头（bow his head before the crowd at once），以后再也不要提起。
bow 意为“鞠躬”，新来的客人每个日子都照例低下在众人面前低下头，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 bows。
bow 意为“鞠躬”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地鞠躬先向最年长的那位鞠躬，用一般过去式 bowed 叙述。
bow 意为“鞠躬”，结尾那句是母亲 1994 年的话：要鞠躬先向最年长的那位鞠躬，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 bow 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1982 the cook bowed to the oldest man first year after year, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook bows to the oldest man first for the whole place whenever the canteen asks.
Bowing to the oldest man first year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever bow his head before the crowd for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen bows his head before the crowd year after year every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother bowed to the oldest man first again, and the canteen remembered that half.
